rv.q: If much of the show’s focus is scattered and its insight unclear, Grody’s point becomes its most legible near her conclusion, when the ruminations find something of a resolution in optimism.

Her intimate delivery, her eye contact with the audience, her informality (she even sits on the edge of the stage during her “conversation” with the audience) make for a delightful theatrical experience.
Playwright Grody has written the workings of her mind into a funny, touching one-act play.

cn.t: Critics praise Kathryn Grody's energetic one-woman show as a wise and rollicking exploration of aging that resonates with contemporary anxieties while celebrating the optimism of staying alive.
